about: Risk profile R4 (docs/risk-profile/01-plan.md, owner decision 2026-11-19): a layered preventive schedule, each item naming its layer. core = USPSTF grade A or B; cardio = ESC/EAS cardiovascular prevention; regional = depends on where the person was born or lives; optional = useful when tracking closely, not a population recommendation (discuss with a doctor). Vaccines follow the US CDC adult schedule. 'interval_months' null = once in adult life. 'methods' lets a screening be done in more than one way, each with its own interval. 'auto' names data that already shows it done (the latest date counts). 'when' narrows who it is for: overweight (BMI 25 or more), ever_smoked, lung_ldct (50-80 with 20 pack-years, current or quit within 15 years: the person confirms), prevent_borderline (PREVENT 10-year total CVD 5 to under 20 %). Not medical advice: the schedule is a reminder of what guidelines say; a doctor decides.

items.name: Blood pressure check
items.source: USPSTF 2021 (A): screen adults 18+, yearly from 40 or at increased risk. A 7-day home series counts.

items.name: Cholesterol test
items.source: USPSTF 2022 (B) statin recommendation assesses lipids from 40 to 75; ACC/AHA: every 4-6 years for adults at low risk.

items.name: Blood glucose (diabetes screen)
items.source: USPSTF 2021 (B): adults 35-70 with overweight or obesity, every 3 years if normal.

items.name: Bowel cancer screening
items.source: USPSTF 2021 (A 50-75, B 45-49): FIT every year or colonoscopy every 10 years, among other options.

items.name: Lung cancer screening (low-dose CT)
items.source: USPSTF 2021 (B): 50-80 with a 20 pack-year history who smoke or quit within 15 years.

items.name: Hepatitis C test
items.source: USPSTF 2020 (B): once for adults 18-79.

items.name: HIV test
items.source: USPSTF 2019 (A): at least once for 15-65; more often with ongoing risk.

items.name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm ultrasound
items.source: USPSTF 2019 (B): once for men 65-75 who have ever smoked.

items.name: Mammogram
items.source: USPSTF 2024 (B): every 2 years from 40 to 74.

items.name: Cervical screening
items.source: USPSTF 2018 (A): cytology every 3 years from 21; from 30, HPV testing every 5 years is an option.

items.name: Bone density (DXA)
items.source: USPSTF 2025 (B): women 65 and older.

items.name: Lipoprotein(a), once
items.source: EAS consensus (Kronenberg et al., Eur Heart J 2022) and ESC/EAS 2019: measure Lp(a) at least once in adult life; it is mostly inherited and the usual lipid panel does not show it.

items.name: Hepatitis B test
items.source: USPSTF 2020 (B): adults born in, or with parents from, regions where 2 % or more carry hepatitis B, which includes East and Southeast Asia.

items.name: Flu vaccine
items.source: CDC adult immunization schedule: every season.

items.name: Tetanus and diphtheria (Td/Tdap) booster
items.source: CDC adult immunization schedule: every 10 years.

items.name: Shingles vaccine (2 doses)
items.source: CDC adult immunization schedule: recombinant zoster vaccine, 2 doses from 50.

items.name: Pneumococcal vaccine
items.source: CDC adult immunization schedule (2024 update): from 50.

items.name: Coronary calcium score (CT)
items.source: ACC/AHA 2019 primary prevention guideline: reasonable when 10-year risk is borderline or intermediate and a treatment decision is uncertain. Discuss with a doctor.

items.name: Dental check-up
items.source: Common practice, 6-12 months; gum disease goes with cardiovascular and metabolic disease.

items.name: Eye examination
items.source: American Academy of Ophthalmology: a baseline exam at 40, then as advised (every 1-2 years from 65).

items.name: Skin check
items.source: USPSTF 2023 (I): evidence insufficient for population screening; worth it with many moles, past sunburns or a family history. Discuss with a doctor.
